idiom_name: single-field wrapper with a private representation and one validating constructor
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare a type that holds exactly one value of the primitive, keep that value private (or protected by the language's opacity mechanism), and expose exactly two operations - a validating constructor that returns the wrapper or an error, and a named accessor for boundary code. Give the wrapper value semantics (equality, hashing, ordering) and keep it immutable. Consumers take the wrapper type in their signatures and never touch the representation, so a raw primitive cannot be passed by accident; if the language offers a transparent or zero-cost form (defined types, opaque types, value/inline classes, repr(transparent) structs), prefer it over a heap-allocating wrapper, and if it offers no distinct-type facility at all, a single-member struct is still stronger than a transparent alias.
code_sketch:
class UserId:                       # one wrapper per concept
    private field raw               # representation hidden
    static parse(raw) -> UserId     # validate + normalise: the only way in
    value() -> RawType              # deliberate exit for boundary code

load_user(id: UserId)               # consumers never see RawType
# load_user("raw-string") is rejected; load_user(order_id) is rejected
pitfalls: Skipping the smart constructor leaves a wrapper that certifies only that a value was boxed, not that it is a legal value of the domain.
Exposing the representation through a public field, an implicit conversion or the language's coercion hooks restores exactly the interchangeability the pattern removed.
Wrapping without value semantics (equality/hash/ordering) makes containers, deduplication and caches behave inconsistently between wrappers.

Wrong move: use a type alias for a domain ID -> the alias remains assignment-compatible with the primitive, so swapped values still compile -> instead define a distinct newtype with explicit construction and conversion.

Wrong move: expose a public raw-field constructor -> callers can bypass the invariant and create invalid values -> instead keep the representation private and admit values through one smart constructor.

Wrong move: add implicit coercions or blanket Deref/forwarding to the wrapped value -> raw values and unrelated wrappers leak through APIs and the boundary becomes invisible -> instead expose only named conversions and deliberately selected operations.
